title: Annotatio VI §.V AD PRIUS: Edite/Hoc — bread (Luther) or spiritual mode already in Jn 6
pass_a_gloss: In vain it is excepted TO THE FORMER: that Spiritual food can also be received corporally and orally when Christ commands it so received, saying: Eat, This is my Body. Reply (a) Christ speaks of the bread, which he understands by This, Luther witnessing in several places — inasmuch as that alone he had taken, broken, and given with corporal hands, saying of the same: This is my body. (b) If likewise Christ spoke of his Body and commanded it to be eaten, he certainly understood no other mode of eating than that taught by himself already before the Holy Supper’s Institution in John 6 — i.e. only the Spiritual.
pass_b_english: AD PRIUS is futile: “Eat, this is my body” does not prove spiritual food is taken corporally/orally.

Either Christ means the bread by “this” (Luther, many places — what hands took, broke, gave), or if he means his body, the eating-mode is the spiritual one he already taught in John 6 before the institution.
source_text: Frustra excipitur AD PRIUS: Spiritualem cibum, etiam corporaliter oraliterque accipi posse, quando à Christo jubetur ita accipi, dicente: Edite, Hoc est Corpus meum. Resp. (a) de pane Christum loqui, quem per Hoc intelligit, teste Luthero pluribus in locis, utpote quem solum corporalibus manibus acceperat, fregerat & dederat, de eodem dicendo: Hoc est corpus meum. (b) Si item de Corpore suo locutus Christus est, & istud edere jussit, utique modum edendi haud alium intellexit, quàm à se, jam ante Cœnæ S. Institutionem, Joh. 6. edoctum, i. e. solum Spiritualem.
notes: AD PRIUS: Hoc=bread or Jn 6 spiritual.
